# reading matrices
To begin the analysis, matricies for each participant are loaded in from the google drive and stored in r's memory to prevent repeated downloading. This resulted in a total of 109 matricies with the dimensions 3080 x 3080

```{r}
# Read the file listing
rds_path <- here("Data", "similarity_matricies.rds")

if(file.exists(rds_path)) {
  matrix_list <- readRDS(rds_path) #reads list of matricies back into memory instead of redownloading if it exists
} else {
  files <- read_csv(here("Data", "similarity_files.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE)
  
  matrix_list <- setNames(
  map(files$id, function(id) {
    url <- paste0("https://drive.usercontent.google.com/download?id=",
      id,"&export=download&confirm=t")
    as.matrix(read.table(url, header = FALSE))
    }),
  toupper(file_path_sans_ext(files$name))
  )
  saveRDS(matrix_list, rds_path)
}
```

## Reading in files with global paths
```{r}
word_file <- here("Data", "kumar_fluencyWords.txt") #path to word list used in fluency/matricies
data_location <- here("Data")
output_location <- here("Analysis", "forager", "output")
domains <- c("animals","authors", "college_majors", "musicians", "sportspersons")
```

## Data Preprocessing
Prior to analysis steps, fluency data was imported and, in accordance with preprocessing, all participants producing less than four responses in any category or lacking a matrix, participant U4TQC9J3, were removed from data sets and further analysis.
```{r}
#reads in fluency data and ensures subject col is text data
fluency_data <- read_csv(here("Data", "cleaned_data", "fluency_data.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(Subject = as.character(Subject))

#participants producing less than four responses in any category discovered and pulled
fluency_number <- fluency_data %>%
  group_by(Subject, domain) %>%
  summarise(item_count = n(), .groups = "drop")

#stores subjects who produced less than four responses
low_response_subjects <- fluency_number %>%
  filter(item_count < 4) %>%
  pull(Subject) %>%
  unique()

#stores subjects whos ID is not in the matrix names
no_matrix_subjects <- fluency_data %>%
  filter(!Subject %in% low_response_subjects) %>%
  pull(Subject) %>%
  unique() %>%
  .[!toupper(.) %in% names(matrix_list)]

no_matrix_subjects

#the pulled participants are filtered out of all defined data sets
excluded_subjects <- unique(c(low_response_subjects, no_matrix_subjects))


fluency_data <- fluency_data %>%
  filter(!Subject %in% excluded_subjects)

tibble(completed = n_distinct(fluency_number$Subject),
       low_response = length(low_response_subjects),
       no_matrix = length(no_matrix_subjects),
       no_valid_pairs = length(setdiff(setdiff(unique(fluency_number$Subject), excluded_subjects),
                                       as.character(valid_rows$subject))),
       analyzed = n_distinct(valid_rows$subject))
```

##Cleaning word list
```{r}
#reading in the fluency word list into a vector, trims spaces/tabs, drops empty lines, creates position vector labeling numbers with corresponding word
words <- read_lines(word_file)
words <- trimws(words)
words <- words[nzchar(words)]

stopifnot(all(vapply(matrix_list, function(m) all(dim(m) == length(words)), logical(1)))) #checks column + row number is equal to the word number

word_index <- setNames(seq_along(words), words)
```

##Helper functions 
```{r}
#Builds tibble recording how many rows a filtering step removed and what percent remained
audit_rows <- function(label, before, after) {
  tibble(step = label,
         rows_before = nrow(before),
         rows_after = nrow(after),
         rows_lost = nrow(before) - nrow(after),
         percent_kept = round(100 * nrow(after) / nrow(before), 1))
}

#Pulls columns, flags missing values, and counts them
na_report <- function(df, cols) {
  tibble(column = cols, 
         num_na = map_int(cols, ~ sum(is.na(df[[.x]]))),
         percent_na = round(100 * num_na / nrow(df), 1))
}

#The first form of word matching, converting to lowercase and removing white space
normalize_word <- function(x) {
  x %>% str_to_lower() %>% str_remove_all("\\s+")
}

#The second form of word matching, stripping accents, making lowercase, and deleting anything that isn't a letter or number
strip_word <- function(x) {
  x %>% stri_trans_general("Latin-ASCII") %>% str_to_lower() %>%
    str_remove_all("[^a-z0-9]")
}
```

##Pairwise Similarity and Domain Processing 
```{r}
#rebuilds the word index with normalized words
word_index <- setNames(seq_along(words), normalize_word(words))

stripped_index <- setNames(seq_along(words), strip_word(words))
stripped_index <- stripped_index[!duplicated(names(stripped_index))]

#corrects words based on first normalization, if failed tries with the second strip then returns matrix positions
lookup_word <- function(x) {
  i <- unname(word_index[normalize_word(x)])
  miss <- is.na(i)
  i[miss] <- unname(stripped_index[strip_word(x[miss])])
  i
}

#looks up matrix position of both previous words and current words and marks which pairs have both items present 
add_pairwise_similarity <- function(group, sim, word_index) {
  group$Previous_Fluency_Item <- lag(group$Fluency_Item) #lag shifts vector down one row so each row has word before it, creating pair
  previous_index <- lookup_word(group$Previous_Fluency_Item)
  current_index <- lookup_word(group$Fluency_Item)
  group$previous_idx <- previous_index
  group$current_idx <- current_index #gives row and column numbers for two words in pair for permutation analysis
  ok <- !is.na(previous_index) & !is.na(current_index)
  
  #creates column filled with NA then fills valid positions
  group$Pairwise_Indv_Similarity <- NA_real_
  group$Pairwise_Indv_Similarity[ok] <- sim[cbind(previous_index[ok], current_index[ok])]
  group
}

#reads in the forager output of a domain, standardizes name and adds domain label. Then splits the data into per participant data frames and finds the participants matrix and adds similarity column
process_domain <- function(domain) {
  path <- file.path(output_location, paste0(domain, "_forager_results"), "lexical_results.csv")
  if(!file.exists(path)) {message("No lexical results for ", domain); return(NULL)}
  
  read_csv(path, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
    rename(subject = Subject) %>%
    mutate(subject = as.character(subject), domain = domain) %>%
    filter(!subject %in% excluded_subjects) %>%
    group_split(subject) %>%
    map(function(g) {
      sim <- matrix_list[[toupper(g$subject[1])]]
      if (is.null(sim)) {message("No matrix for ", g$subject[1]); return(NULL)}
      add_pairwise_similarity(g, sim, word_index)
    }) %>%
    bind_rows()
}

#returns (1) total row #, count of how many items were the first, lacking a previous word, and how many pairs are missing a word from word list, (2) the number of pairs per domain, how many have NA individual similarity cols, and (3) a per domain individual pairwise similarity file 
complete_similarities <- map_dfr(domains, process_domain)

complete_similarities %>% 
  summarise(
    total = n(),
    first_item = sum(is.na(Previous_Fluency_Item)),
    not_in_word_list = sum(!is.na(Previous_Fluency_Item) &
                             (is.na(lookup_word(Fluency_Item)) | is.na(lookup_word(Previous_Fluency_Item)))))
  

complete_similarities %>%
  filter(!is.na(Previous_Fluency_Item)) %>%
  group_by(domain) %>%
  summarise(pairs = n(),
            missing = sum(is.na(Pairwise_Indv_Similarity)),
            pct_missing = round(100 * missing / pairs, 1))

complete_similarities %>% 
  group_split(domain) %>%
  walk(function(d) {
    write_csv(d %>% rename(Subject = subject) %>% select(-domain),
              file.path(output_location, paste0(d$domain[1], "_forager_results"), "lexical_results_indv_pairwise_similarity.csv"))
  })
```


## SpAM Analysis

First, both general semantic similarity, based on the matricies from a general text corpora, and individual semantic similarity, based on the unweighted matricies from a participant's input subreddits, were correlated with euclidean distances pulled from each participant's SpAM response and pooled. This analysis revealed both general and individual semantic similarity correlated negatively with euclidean distance, yet the general semantic similarity had a more negative, moderate association (r = -0.392) compared to individual semantic similarity (r = -0.218).

```{r}
#translates what participant types in fluency to corrected response used by forager, keeping rows where both words exist and the typed word differs from the corrected one 
corrections <- fluency_data %>%
  transmute(subject = as.character(Subject),
            domain, spam_word = response, forager_word = corrected_response) %>%
  filter(!is.na(spam_word), !is.na(forager_word), 
         strip_word(spam_word) != strip_word(forager_word)) %>%
           distinct()
  nrow(corrections)
  
  corrections %>% slice_sample(n = 30)
  corrections %>% count(subject, domain, spam_word) %>% filter(n > 1)

  #read in SpAM pairwise distances         
spatial_distances <- read_csv(here("Data", "raw_data", "organized_spam.csv"), show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(subject = as.character(subject)) %>%
  filter(!subject %in% excluded_subjects)

#attaches corrections to both words, uses correction if needed
spatial_distances_fixed <- spatial_distances %>%
  left_join(corrections %>% rename(word1 = spam_word, w1_fix = forager_word), 
            by = c("subject", "domain", "word1")) %>%
  left_join(corrections %>% rename(word2 = spam_word, w2_fix = forager_word), 
            by = c("subject", "domain", "word2")) %>%
  mutate(w1 = strip_word(coalesce(w1_fix, word1)),
         w2 = strip_word(coalesce(w2_fix, word2)))

similarities <- complete_similarities %>%
  mutate(w1 = strip_word(Previous_Fluency_Item),
         w2 = strip_word(Fluency_Item),
         matched = TRUE) %>%
  select(subject, domain, w1, w2, previous_idx, current_idx,
         Pairwise_Indv_Similarity, matched)

merged_sim_spam_data <- spatial_distances_fixed %>%
  left_join(similarities, by = c("subject", "domain", "w1", "w2"))

nrow(merged_sim_spam_data) == nrow(spatial_distances)   # must print TRUE

unmatched <- merged_sim_spam_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(word1), !is.na(word2), is.na(matched)) %>%
  select(subject, domain, word1, word2)

na_report(merged_sim_spam_data, c("euclidean_distance", "Pairwise_Indv_Similarity"))

valid_rows <- merged_sim_spam_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(euclidean_distance), !is.na(Pairwise_Indv_Similarity))

#checks loss
audit_rows("valid_rows filter", merged_sim_spam_data, valid_rows)
valid_rows %>% count(domain)
n_distinct(valid_rows$subject)

#list of words actually produced by each person in each domain then checks missing values and reason for missing
present <- complete_similarities %>%
  distinct(subject, domain, key = strip_word(Fluency_Item))

unmatched_diagram <- merged_sim_spam_data %>%
  filter(!is.na(word1), !is.na(word2), is.na(Semantic_Similarity)) %>%
  left_join(present %>% mutate(w1_in = TRUE),
            by = c("subject", "domain", "w1" = "key")) %>%
  left_join(present %>% mutate(w2_in = TRUE),
            by = c("subject", "domain", "w2" = "key")) %>%
  mutate(w1_in = coalesce(w1_in, FALSE),
         w2_in = coalesce(w2_in, FALSE),
         reason = case_when(w1_in & w2_in ~ "both in forager, not consecutive",
                            !w1_in & !w2_in ~ "both missing from forager",
                            TRUE ~ "one word missing from forager"))

count(unmatched_diagram, domain, reason)

#checks for nonexistent corrections
fluency_data %>%
  filter(is.na(corrected_response) | corrected_response == "") %>%
  count(domain)
```

```{r}
subjects <- unique(valid_rows$subject)
sims_by_subject <- map(subjects, function(s) {
  d <- valid_rows %>% filter(subject == s)
  idx <- cbind(d$previous_idx, d$current_idx)
  others <- setdiff(names(matrix_list), toupper(s))
  vapply(others, function(id) matrix_list[[id]][idx], numeric(nrow(d)))
}) %>% setNames(subjects)

spam_data <- map_dfr(subjects, function(s) {
  valid_rows %>% filter(subject == s) %>%
    mutate(individual_similarity = Pairwise_Indv_Similarity,
           consensus_similarity = rowMeans(sims_by_subject[[s]]))
}) %>% mutate(subject = factor(subject), domain = factor(domain))

fit <- function(f, d) lmer(f, data = d, REML = FALSE)
r2m <- function(m) performance::r2_nakagawa(m)$R2_marginal
r2c <- function(m) performance::r2_nakagawa(m)$R2_conditional

model_spam_base      <- fit(euclidean_distance ~ domain + (1 | subject), spam_data)
model_spam_indiv     <- fit(euclidean_distance ~ individual_similarity * domain + (1 | subject), spam_data)
model_spam_consensus <- fit(euclidean_distance ~ consensus_similarity * domain + (1 | subject), spam_data)

# Swapped: one random donor per participant per draw, refit 100 times
set.seed(2026)
draw_swapped <- function() unlist(lapply(subjects, function(s) {
  m <- sims_by_subject[[s]]; m[, sample(ncol(m), 1)]
}), use.names = FALSE)

swap_r2 <- map_dfr(1:100, function(k) {
  d <- spam_data; d$swapped_similarity <- draw_swapped()
  m <- fit(euclidean_distance ~ swapped_similarity * domain + (1 | subject), d)
  tibble(draw = k, marginal = r2m(m), conditional = r2c(m))
})

spam_r2 <- tibble(
  measure = c("Domain only", "Swapped (mean of 100)", "Own", "Consensus"),
  marginal = c(r2m(model_spam_base), mean(swap_r2$marginal), r2m(model_spam_indiv), r2m(model_spam_consensus)),
  conditional = c(r2c(model_spam_base), mean(swap_r2$conditional), r2c(model_spam_indiv), r2c(model_spam_consensus)))
spam_r2

# does Own beat a random stranger's matrix?
(1 + sum(swap_r2$marginal >= r2m(model_spam_indiv))) / (1 + nrow(swap_r2))

```
```{r}
set.seed(2026)
swaps <- replicate(100, draw_swapped(), simplify = FALSE)   # one random stranger per participant per draw

domain_r2_models <- map_dfr(levels(spam_data$domain), function(dom) {
  keep <- spam_data$domain == dom
  d <- droplevels(spam_data[keep, ])

  own  <- r2m(fit(euclidean_distance ~ individual_similarity + (1 | subject), d))
  cons <- r2m(fit(euclidean_distance ~ consensus_similarity + (1 | subject), d))
  sw   <- map_dbl(swaps, function(s) {
            d$swapped_similarity <- s[keep]
            r2m(fit(euclidean_distance ~ swapped_similarity + (1 | subject), d)) })

  tibble(domain = dom, n_pairs = nrow(d),
         Swapped = mean(sw), Own = own, Consensus = cons,
         own_vs_swap_p = (1 + sum(sw >= own)) / (1 + length(sw)))
}) %>% mutate(own_vs_swap_p_holm = p.adjust(own_vs_swap_p, method = "holm"))

domain_r2_models

```
```{r}
domain_r2_models %>%
  pivot_longer(c(Swapped, Own, Consensus), names_to = "measure", values_to = "marginal") %>%
  mutate(measure = factor(measure, levels = c("Swapped", "Own", "Consensus")),
         domain_label = paste0(str_replace(domain, "_", " "), "\n(", n_pairs, " pairs)")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(domain_label, marginal, fill = measure)) +
  geom_col(position = position_dodge(width = .8), width = .7) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Variance explained (marginal R²)", fill = NULL, title = NULL) +
  poster_theme + theme(legend.position = "bottom", text = element_text(size = 12))
```


#Group mean permutation analysis


```{r}
leaving_one_out_results <- map_dfr(subjects, function(current_subject) {
  subject_data <- valid_rows %>% filter(subject == current_subject)
  idx <- cbind(subject_data$previous_idx, subject_data$current_idx)
  others <- setdiff(names(matrix_list), toupper(current_subject))
  
  sims <- vapply(others, function(donor_id) matrix_list[[donor_id]][idx], numeric(nrow(subject_data)))
  leave_one_out_mean <- rowMeans(sims)
  
  tibble(subject = current_subject, 
         own_correlation = cor(subject_data$euclidean_distance,
                               subject_data$Pairwise_Indv_Similarity),
         leaving_one_out_correlation = cor(subject_data$euclidean_distance,
                               leave_one_out_mean),
         general_correlation = cor(subject_data$euclidean_distance,
                               subject_data$Semantic_Similarity))
})

```


```{r}
leaving_one_out_results %>%
  summarise(across(c(own_correlation, leaving_one_out_correlation, general_correlation), list(mean = mean, median = median)))

t.test(leaving_one_out_results$own_correlation, leaving_one_out_results$leaving_one_out_correlation, paired = TRUE)
t.test(leaving_one_out_results$leaving_one_out_correlation, leaving_one_out_results$general_correlation, paired = TRUE)

```


```{r}
plot_r2 <- function(r2_tbl, ymax) {
  base <- r2_tbl$marginal[r2_tbl$measure == "Domain only"]
  r2_tbl %>%
    filter(measure != "Domain only") %>%
    mutate(measure = factor(recode(measure, "Swapped (mean of 100)" = "Swapped"),
                            levels = c("Swapped", "Own", "Consensus"))) %>%
    ggplot(aes(measure, marginal, fill = measure)) +
    geom_col(width = .6) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = base, linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.3f", marginal)), vjust = -0.4, size = 8) +
    scale_fill_manual(values = pal) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, ymax)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Variance explained (marginal R²)", title = NULL) +
    poster_theme + theme(text = element_text(size = 18))
}

fig1 <- plot_r2(spam_r2, 0.13)
ggsave("fig1_spam_r2.png", fig1, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 300)
```

```{r}
domain_r2 <- map_dfr(domain_cells, function(cell) {
  s <- cell$summary
  tibble(subject = s$subject, domain = s$domain, num_pairs = s$num_pairs,
         Own       = s$own_correlation^2,
         Consensus = s$leave_one_out_correlation^2,
         Swapped   = mean(cell$permutation_correlation^2, na.rm = TRUE))
}) %>% drop_na()

domain_r2_plot_data <- domain_r2 %>%
  pivot_longer(c(Swapped, Own, Consensus), names_to = "measure", values_to = "R2") %>%
  mutate(measure = factor(measure, levels = c("Swapped", "Own", "Consensus"))) %>%
  group_by(domain, measure) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), mean_R2 = mean(R2), se = sd(R2) / sqrt(n), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(lo = pmax(mean_R2 - qt(.975, n - 1) * se, 0),
         hi = mean_R2 + qt(.975, n - 1) * se,
         domain_label = paste0(str_replace(domain, "_", " "), "\n(n = ", n, ")"))
```


## Fluency Analysis


```{r}
# each participant's mean individual similarity per domain
subject_mean_similarity <- valid_rows %>%
  mutate(subject = as.character(subject)) %>%
  group_by(subject, domain) %>%
  summarise(individual_mean = mean(Pairwise_Indv_Similarity, na.rm = TRUE),
            n_items = n(),
            .groups = "drop")

# fluency count per participant and domain
fluency <- read_csv(file.path(data_location, "raw_data", "organized_fluency.csv"),
                    show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(subject = as.character(subject))

fluency_count <- fluency %>%
  group_by(subject, domain) %>%
  summarise(fluency_count = n(), .groups = "drop")

merged_similarity_fluency <- subject_mean_similarity %>%
  inner_join(fluency_count, by = c("subject", "domain")) %>%
  filter(n_items >= 2)

# loss checks
audit_rows("subject_mean_similarity x fluency_count", subject_mean_similarity, merged_similarity_fluency)
anti_join(subject_mean_similarity, fluency_count, by = c("subject", "domain"))

# within-domain correlations (individual similarity only)
domain_fluency_correlations <- merged_similarity_fluency %>%
  group_by(domain) %>%
  filter(n() >= 5) %>%
  summarise(num_subjects = n(),
            individual_cor = cor(fluency_count, individual_mean),
            .groups = "drop")

print(domain_fluency_correlations, n = Inf)
```

#Fluency analysis testing fluency count correlation with similarity for general and individual
```{r}
#fluency relationship across domains
fluency_model_data <- merged_similarity_fluency %>%
  group_by(domain) %>%
  mutate(fluency_z = as.numeric(scale(fluency_count))) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(subject = factor(subject), domain = factor(domain))

model_indv_main <- lmer(individual_mean ~ fluency_z + domain + (1 | subject), data = fluency_model_data)
model_indv_int  <- lmer(individual_mean ~ fluency_z * domain + (1 | subject), data = fluency_model_data)
anova(model_indv_main, model_indv_int)

# overall within-domain association (replaces the confounded pooled r)
summary(model_indv_main)$coefficients["fluency_z", ]

# which domains differ from zero? Holm over 5 tests
domain_cor_p <- merged_similarity_fluency %>%
  group_by(domain) %>%
  summarise(individual_r = cor(fluency_count, individual_mean),
            individual_p = cor.test(fluency_count, individual_mean)$p.value,
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(p_holm = p.adjust(individual_p, method = "holm"))

domain_cor_p

```


```{r}
set.seed(2026)
fluency <- read_csv(file.path(data_location, "raw_data", "organized_fluency.csv"),
                    show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(subject = as.character(subject))

fluency_count <- fluency %>%
  group_by(subject, domain) %>%
  summarise(fluency_count = n(), .groups = "drop")
# similarity for every valid pair under Own, Consensus, and 100 random strangers
pair_sims <- map_dfr(subjects, function(s) {
  d <- valid_rows %>% filter(subject == s)
  idx <- cbind(d$previous_idx, d$current_idx)
  others <- setdiff(names(matrix_list), toupper(s))
  sims <- vapply(others, function(id) matrix_list[[id]][idx], numeric(nrow(d)))
  swaps <- as_tibble(sims[, sample(ncol(sims), 100), drop = FALSE],
                     .name_repair = ~ paste0("swap", seq_along(.x)))
  bind_cols(tibble(subject = s, domain = d$domain,
                   own = d$Pairwise_Indv_Similarity,
                   consensus = rowMeans(sims)),
            swaps)
})

# mean similarity per participant and domain, joined to fluency counts
fluency_all <- pair_sims %>%
  group_by(subject, domain) %>%
  summarise(across(c(own, consensus, starts_with("swap")), mean),
            n_items = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  inner_join(fluency_count, by = c("subject", "domain")) %>%
  filter(n_items >= 2)

fluency_fit <- fluency_all %>% mutate(subject = factor(subject), domain = factor(domain))

model_fluency_base      <- fit(fluency_count ~ domain + (1 | subject), fluency_fit)
model_fluency_indiv     <- fit(fluency_count ~ own * domain + (1 | subject), fluency_fit)
model_fluency_consensus <- fit(fluency_count ~ consensus * domain + (1 | subject), fluency_fit)

swap_fluency_r2 <- map_dfr(1:100, function(k) {
  d <- fluency_fit; d$swapped <- d[[paste0("swap", k)]]
  m <- fit(fluency_count ~ swapped * domain + (1 | subject), d)
  tibble(draw = k, marginal = r2m(m), conditional = r2c(m))
})

fluency_r2 <- tibble(
  measure = c("Domain only", "Swapped (mean of 100)", "Own", "Consensus"),
  marginal = c(r2m(model_fluency_base), mean(swap_fluency_r2$marginal), r2m(model_fluency_indiv), r2m(model_fluency_consensus)),
  conditional = c(r2c(model_fluency_base), mean(swap_fluency_r2$conditional), r2c(model_fluency_indiv), r2c(model_fluency_consensus)))
fluency_r2

(1 + sum(swap_fluency_r2$marginal >= r2m(model_fluency_indiv))) / (1 + nrow(swap_fluency_r2))
```


```{r}
fig3 <- fluency_r2 %>%
  mutate(gain = marginal - marginal[measure == "Domain only"]) %>%
  filter(measure != "Domain only") %>%
  mutate(measure = factor(recode(measure, "Swapped (mean of 100)" = "Swapped"),
                          levels = c("Swapped", "Own", "Consensus"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(measure, gain, fill = measure)) +
  geom_col(width = .6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("+%.3f", gain)), vjust = -0.4, size = 8) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pal) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 0.02)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "R² gained over domain alone", title = NULL) +
  poster_theme + theme(text = element_text(size = 18))

ggsave("fig3_fluency_gain.png", fig3, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 300)
```

## Word Fluency Examination

After conducting these analyses, especially the domain analyses revealing the number of complete observations available at the domain level being as low as 2 for authors and sportspersons, I investigated the fluency lists provided for each participant to see how well words were represented generally. This analysis revealed a that out of the total of 9,002,419 rows,or participant/word/frequency value combinations, there were 3,257,027 words with a frequency of 0, accounting for ~36.2% of the frequency data. 

I wonder if this may indicate that the participant level corpera is not properly covering all of a participants individual words/interests and if his leads to the semantic estimates lacking accuracy, specifically for rare or underepresented words.

It was stated that the email sent accompanying the matricies that if a word was not represented in the corpus its similarity was set to 0, so it could be possible that words are misinterpreted as being unrelated when they are just not present.

```{r}#
frequency_dir <- here("Data", "kumar_freqs")

if (!dir.exists(frequency_dir)) {
  zip_path <- here("Data", "kumar_freqs.zip")
  download.file("https://drive.usercontent.google.com/download?id=1CCzAThSr95yNf_n3ANcAzto_vWZpf4tZ&export=download&confirm=t", zip_path, mode = "wb")
  unzip(zip_path, exdir = here("Data"))
}

frequency_files <- list.files(frequency_dir, pattern = "\\.csv$", full.names = TRUE, recursive = TRUE)

frequency_data <- map_dfr(frequency_files, function(f) {
  read_csv(f, show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
    mutate(Subject = toupper(file_path_sans_ext(basename(f))))
}) %>%
  mutate(Subject = as.character(Subject),
         word = as.character(word),
         frequency = as.numeric(frequency))

overall_frequency <- frequency_data %>%
  summarise(total_rows = n(), 
            n_subjects = n_distinct(Subject),
            n_unique_words = n_distinct(word),
            n_zero_frequency = sum(frequency == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
            n_missing_frequency = sum(is.na(frequency)),
            percent_zero_frequency = mean(frequency == 0, na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
            median_frequency = median(frequency, na.rm = TRUE),
            mean_frequency = mean(frequency, na.rm = TRUE),
            n_low_frequency = sum(frequency > 0 & frequency <= 5,
                                  na.rm = TRUE))

overall_frequency

frequency_data %>%
  mutate(frequency_group = if_else(
    frequency == 0, "Zero", "Positive"
  )) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = frequency_group, fill = frequency_group)) + geom_bar() +
  labs(
    title = "Frequency rows: zero vs present", 
    x = "Frequency category",
    y = "number of rows",
    fill = "Frequency"
  ) + theme_minimal() + theme(legend.position = "none")
```

I looked at this on the participant level and found that the percentage of zero frequency words ranged across participants from 25.6% to 72.2% so some participants could have semantic similarity measures which are more or less effected. Also, looking back at the domains pairs able to be analyzed, for domains containing the most unique entries like sportspersons and authors, there were very very few pairs that could be properly compared.

```{r}#
participant_frequency <- frequency_data %>%
  group_by(Subject) %>%
  summarise(total_rows = n(),
            zero_frequency = sum(frequency == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
            percent_zero = mean(frequency == 0, na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
            low_frequency = sum(frequency > 0 & frequency <= 5, na.rm = TRUE),
            percent_low_frequency = mean(frequency > 0 & frequency <= 5, na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
            median_frequency = median(frequency, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(percent_zero))
participant_frequency

participant_frequency %>%
  summarise(
    n_subjects = n(),
    min_percent_zero = min(percent_zero),
    median_percent_zero = median(percent_zero),
    mean_percent_zero = mean(percent_zero),
    max_percent_zero = max(percent_zero),
    st_percent_zero = sd(percent_zero)
  )

ggplot(
  participant_frequency, aes(x = reorder(Subject, percent_zero), y = percent_zero)) +
         geom_col(fill = "steelblue") +
         geom_hline(yintercept = median(participant_frequency$percent_zero), linetype = "dashed") +
         coord_flip() + labs(title = "Zero frequency rows by participant", subtitle = "dashed line = median", x = "Participant", y = "Zero frequency rows (%)") + theme_minimal() + theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 3))
```
